newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl sees improvement in German jobless by mid-97.
newsitem.headline: Kohl sees improvement in German jobless by mid-97.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Friday that the second half of 1997 would see an improvement in Germany's jobless situation, but said that halving German unemployment by 2000 was a "goal", not a forecast.

"We are looking at developments which should lead to an improvement in the employment situation by the middle of 1997," Kohl told a news conference after a one-day meeting with Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

Kohl said halving unemployment by the turn of the century was still "a goal," but added that it had not been a fixed forecast as widely reported and said he never intended it to be understood as a forecast for German unemployment.
On Thursday the jobless rate in Germany reached a post-war record of 12.2 percent, with an unadjusted total of 4.658 million people out of work.
